extracted.intended_audience: general readers / non-mathematicians interested in mathematics
extracted.subtask_description: Writing or presenting mathematics for a non-specialist audience in a way that reveals and communicates its aesthetic qualities. Emphasises criteria that make mathematics feel beautiful and accessible without requiring advanced technical background.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elegance / efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Solutions that avoid unnecessary complexity and capture "the essence of the ideas."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise arguments that do not introduce extraneous machinery; seek proofs or explanations that are streamlined and show the core structure of the idea rather than cumbersome casework or technical baggage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanatory power
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematics that reveals why something works, not merely that it works. "This is critical to mathematicians."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to show underlying reasons and mechanisms. Prefer explanations that illuminate relationships and causes rather than giving only verification or calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalisability
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments that extend neatly from specific cases to universal principles "without drawing the dots" for each instance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor approaches that make patterns and structures clear so the reader can see how the idea scales or applies in broader contexts, rather than presenting isolated examples that must each be separately justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy of expression
rubrics_metrics.description: "A single diagram captures everything we need to know."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concise representations (diagrams, definitions, statements) that encapsulate much information at once. Strive for compactness in presentation so a single clear image or short formulation conveys the concept effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memorability
rubrics_metrics.description: Solutions create lasting impressions through visual or conceptual clarity rather than rote formula memorisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design explanations and examples that stick — leverage striking visuals, simple metaphors, or conceptual pivots that make the idea easy to recall and re-use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility with depth
rubrics_metrics.description: Beauty doesn't require university-level sophistication; elegant problems exist at school level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose examples and explanations that are approachable for non-specialists while still containing substantive insight. Show depth without relying on advanced technical machinery; present layers that beginners can appreciate and experts can recognise as rich.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveat: understanding first
rubrics_metrics.description: Appreciating math beauty requires understanding first — like appreciating sophisticated music or visual art. Beauty emerges through engagement and exploration, not passive observation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expect instantaneous aesthetic appreciation; provide the conceptual scaffolding and prerequisites the audience needs. Encourage active engagement (worked examples, progressive buildup) so readers can experience the emergence of beauty themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implication for exposition: teach prerequisites
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'good' piece of mathematical writing teaches the prerequisites needed to appreciate its own elegance. Without that scaffolding, the beauty is invisible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When presenting elegant mathematics, explicitly teach or reveal the minimal background and intermediate steps required for the target audience to perceive the elegance. Structure the exposition so appreciation is an attainable outcome of reading, not a precondition.
